title: Accessible inverse images of replete arrow subcategories
statement: Work with small Hom sets in a fixed universe, and colimits as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. A category is locally presentable if it is cocomplete and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa$, generated under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects $P$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves these colimits. Here $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has cardinality less than $\kappa$. Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be locally presentable categories and $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a functor preserving small $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular $\kappa$. Write $\mathcal C^{[1]}$ and $\mathcal D^{[1]}$ for their arrow categories, whose arrows are commuting squares and whose colimits are computed at source and target. A replete full subcategory $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D$ is an accessible subcategory if, for some infinite regular $\lambda$, it is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits computed in $\mathcal D$ and is generated under those colimits by a small set of its objects. Replete means closed under isomorphism in $\mathcal D$. If $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D^{[1]}$ is an accessible subcategory, the replete full subcategory of $\mathcal C^{[1]}$ on arrows $f$ such that $F(f)\in\mathcal V$ is accessible. No assertion is made that the same cardinal works for every $F$ or every $\mathcal V$.
